_comment: Provenance for ism-controls.json, which is stored byte-for-byte as retrieved so the
mapping in docs/LLD-RHEL-IRAP.md is reproducible. JSON has no comment syntax, so the
header lives in this sidecar file rather than in the dataset itself.
THE CURRENTLY PUBLISHED ISM (cyber.gov.au) IS AUTHORITATIVE. Control numbers, wording
and applicability drift between quarterly ISM releases; re-retrieve and re-check before
relying on this mapping for an assessment. See docs/ISM.md for the refresh procedure.
THIS IS A THIRD-PARTY COMMUNITY EXTRACT, NOT AN ACSC PUBLICATION, and it carries no ISM
release label — so the mapping cannot claim to be any specific quarterly edition. Replacing
it with the official XLSX/OSCAL release is a data change only: swap the file, update this
sidecar, re-run scripts/ism_map.py and resolve whatever ids it reports as missing.
source_authority: third-party community extract; not published, endorsed or maintained by ACSC/ASD
format: object mapping control id (ism-NNNN / ism-principle-XN) to the control statement, with some HTML markup embedded
normalisation_note: 36 values carry the NEXT control appended after a stray markdown table separator, e.g. '... | | [ism-0430](/control/ism-0430) | Access to systems ...'. scripts/ism_map.py splits these back out at load time; the raw file is left untouched.
